properties.description:
DETECTS
Any monitored host that has not sent a Heartbeat record for 30 minutes or more, evaluated every 30 minutes.

WHY IT MATTERS
A detection-coverage control rather than a threat detection. A silent agent means the SOC is blind to that host: no Syslog, no security events, no telemetry feeding any other rule in this workspace. Attackers stop or uninstall monitoring agents specifically to suppress logging before acting (MITRE T1489, Service Stop). The far more common cause is a host being shut down, deallocated, or losing connectivity.

TRIAGE
1. Check whether the VM is running or deallocated in Azure.
2. If running but silent, connect and verify the Azure Monitor Agent service state.
3. Review the last events received before the gap for signs of tampering or a service stop.
4. Correlate against the Linux logging service rule. Both firing for one host indicates deliberate action.
5. Restore agent connectivity and confirm ingestion resumes.

FALSE POSITIVES
Expected and frequent in a lab. Auto-shutdown schedules, deallocated VMs, and decommissioned hosts all trigger it. Tune by excluding hosts on a known shutdown schedule or lengthening the threshold.

SOURCE
Heartbeat
properties.query:
Heartbeat
| summarize LastHeartbeat = max(TimeGenerated), OSType = any(OSType), ComputerIP = any(ComputerIP) by Computer
| where LastHeartbeat < ago(30m)
| extend MinutesSilent = datetime_diff("minute", now(), LastHeartbeat)
| extend TimeGenerated = LastHeartbeat, HostName = Computer

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{Computer}} last sent a heartbeat at {{LastHeartbeat}}, {{MinutesSilent}} minutes ago. Telemetry from this host is not reaching the workspace.
